items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I think one of those quotes was from Scott Yanow.

ctx.x: I wanted to read something. These are two different quotes about you, and it caught my eye because one is from the Grove Encyclopedia of Jazz and it’s talking about you and then, “he has few peers on ‘Cherokee’.” And then there’s another thing from another book about recordings, it says, “‘Cherokee’ is a song he practically owns.” What’s this thing with “Cherokee” now?

Well you know when I was coming up, “Cherokee” was something you had to conquer, much like — now my memory is leaving me, I’m having a senior moment — no you know like “Giant Steps” — much like “Giant Steps” was a couple of decades later. There are tunes like that floating around, like “Cherokee,” “Giant Steps,” “Stella By Starlight,” things that have a lot of changes and move around. So I worked hard on that, and I recorded it first with Maynard on “The New Sounds of Maynard Ferguson,” and then I recorded it…

“Koko” on an album I did for Palo Alto Records and I recorded “Cherokee” on that VSOP album, and then I just did one that’s supposed to come out on that Fresh Sounds, that Spanish label out of Barcelona, that’s called “A Suite for Yardbird,” they’re all Bird tunes, and I did “Koko” again because the producer wanted me to do it, so who am I to argue with the producer so I did it. So I guess I played it so much. I don’t really claim to be the master of “Cherokee,” there’s a lot of people that — I mean anybody who’s…
